$comment: Auto-discovery addresses found outside the catalogues tools/discover_networks.py
reads on its own — SPEC.md §4.1.
The survey starts from MobilityData's systems.csv, the registry the GBFS
standard keeps of itself, and from France's national access point. Neither
is exhaustive: a registry lags behind the networks it describes, and a
country without a national access point has none at all. What they leave
out is listed here, one entry per network, each carrying the public page it
was read from — an operator's developer page, a city's open-data portal —
so that the claim can be checked by whoever doubts it.
NOTHING IS TRUSTED FOR HAVING BEEN WRITTEN HERE. The address is called and
judged exactly like any other: a feed listed below that turns out to be
free-floating, or behind a key, or gone, is set aside in the report like
the rest. And no address is ever invented: §4.1 forbids guessing a
`gbfs.json` URL, and a URL that answers is not the same thing as a URL a
producer published.
WHAT WAS LOOKED FOR AND NOT RETAINED, so the search is not started again
from nothing:
· Taiwan — YouBike runs some fifteen conurbations, Taipei and Kaohsiung
among them, and publishes their availability on the national open-data
portal. The format is its own JSON, not GBFS, and this application
reads GBFS (§4.1). Nothing here can be done about it but wait.
· South Korea — Seoul's Ttareungi, Daejeon's Tashu, Changwon's Nubija:
open data, on portals that issue a key per caller. §2 forbids the
application to hard-code a secret.
· India — the Chartered Bike networks (Surat, Ranchi, Bhopal…) publish no
open feed of their stations.
· China — the municipal systems of Xi'an, Aksu and Putian likewise.
· Kazakhstan, Georgia, Ecuador, Peru, Malta, Montenegro, Costa Rica —
each runs one docked network whose availability is served to its own
application alone.
Re-running the survey is what settles whether any of that is still true.
Shape of an entry:
id            identifier of the system, free but stable
country       ISO 3166-1 alpha-2
name          the network's name, as its producer writes it
location      the conurbation, as the producer names it
discoveryUrl  the gbfs.json address, and that alone (§4.1)
source        where this address was read — the page, not the feed
publisher     the authority that opened the data, for the credit (§4.5)
licence       its licence identifier, if the producer states one
datasetPageUrl  the page a user can be sent to for the licence
